name: Single-Leg Slider Hamstring Curl
summary: A challenging unilateral bodyweight exercise that strengthens the hamstrings through knee flexion while isometrically engaging the glutes to keep the hips elevated.

setup: Lie flat on your back with your arms resting at your sides, palms pressing into the floor for support.
Place the heel of the working foot onto a slider with your ankle dorsiflexed.
Bend the non-working knee and elevate that foot off the floor, holding it near your chest or keeping the knee bent at ninety degrees.
Engage your glutes and drive through the working heel to bridge your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your working knee.
steps: Slowly extend your working knee by sliding your heel away from your body in a controlled manner.
Continue sliding until your leg is almost completely straight, keeping your hips elevated off the floor.
Dig your heel firmly into the slider and contract your hamstrings to pull the heel back toward your glutes.
Drive your hips up at the top of the curl to re-establish full hip extension before beginning the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you extend the leg and slide the heel out; exhale forcefully as you curl the heel back in toward your glutes.

common_faults.correction: Squeeze the working glute continuously to prevent the pelvis from dropping toward the ground as the leg straightens.

common_faults.fault: Sliding out too fast without control
common_faults.correction: Resist the movement during the eccentric phase, taking two to three seconds to slide outward smoothly.

common_faults.fault: Pushing with the toes instead of the heel
common_faults.correction: Keep your toes pointed upward and focus pressure directly through the center of your heel.

precautions: Warm up the hamstrings thoroughly before performing this exercise to reduce the risk of muscle cramps or strains.
